summary: FieldShift turns NASA Earth observation data into a six-season crop rotation plan for one farmer's own field in Bangladesh. In the drought-prone Barind region, NASA's GRACE-FO shows water storage falling about 1 cm per year, while a typical Boro rice rotation pumps about 1,121 mm of groundwater a year and leaves fields bare for 115 days. A farmer pins the field on satellite imagery; FieldShift reads NASA POWER weather and GPM IMERG rainfall for that exact point, computes each crop's water need with the FAO-56 method, and a mixed-integer optimizer (MILP) picks the best rotation within the farmer's limits. On our demo field, the Balanced plan cuts irrigation from 1,121 to 340 mm a year (about 70%), cuts bare days from 115 to 60 and adds nitrogen through legumes. Plans can be stress-tested against heatwave, drought, flood, cold and salinity, and re-planned after every real harvest. FieldShift answers the Field Shift challenge by giving farmers field-level, data-driven decisions to adapt to a changing climate.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

FieldShift is a decision-support tool that turns NASA Earth observations into a six-season (two-year) crop rotation plan for one farmer's own field. It compares the farmer's current rotation with four strategies – Balanced, Profit, Water saving and Soil health – and explains the water, soil and income trade-offs of each.

THE PROBLEM IT ANSWERS

In Bangladesh's drought-prone Barind region, NASA's GRACE-FO shows water storage falling about 1 cm per year. A typical Boro rice → Fallow → Aman rotation pumps about 1,121 mm of groundwater a year, leaves fields bare for about 115 days and returns no nitrogen to the soil, while heat and dry spells hit at the wrong time. One piece of advice for the whole country does not fit: Barind, the haor wetlands and the coast each face different water, soil and weather.

HOW IT WORKS

1. My Fields – the farmer pins the field on satellite imagery, with area, irrigation capacity and current rotation. Soil texture, field capacity and wilting point come from ISRIC SoilGrids, each marked as measured or estimated.

2. Rotation Planner – for the field's coordinates, FieldShift reads NASA POWER daily weather and GPM IMERG daily rainfall, runs an FAO-56 Penman-Monteith daily water balance for each crop and season, and solves a PuLP mixed-integer linear program (MILP) to choose the best rotation. The farmer sets priorities and constraints: goal, water available (full, limited, rainfed), no power tiller, crops they cannot sell. No crop family is repeated back-to-back, which breaks pest and disease cycles.

3. Climate stress test – heatwave, drought, flood, cold wave and salinity at different intensities, using FAO-33 yield-response factors, season by season.

4. Adaptive replan – after each harvest the farmer enters the real yield and price; FieldShift recalibrates and re-optimizes the remaining seasons, explaining what changed and why.

5. Climate & Risk – a month-by-month risk calendar from 24 years of NASA data, trends with significance tests, the GRACE-FO groundwater trend, and the last 30 days compared with normal.

6. Water – seasonal water budget, pump runtime, AWD guidance and a daily irrigation schedule.

7. Market & Profit – season costs, revenue and break-even prices from DAM Bangladesh rates, with a ±20% price test.

8. Evidence & Method – every number traced to its data source, with honest limits.

An in-app assistant answers questions in Bangla or English.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

On our demo field (Chapainawabganj, Barind), the Balanced plan (Mustard → Soybean → Aman → Chickpea → Sesame → Aman) cuts irrigation from 1,121 to 340 mm a year (about 70%), bare days from 115 to 60, and adds about 35 kg N/ha through legumes, while expected profit nearly doubles and stays ahead with a 20% price drop. The intended impact is less groundwater pumping, healthier soil and more resilient farm income, field by field.

TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGIES

Python, FastAPI, PuLP (MILP), pandas/NumPy, earthaccess and OPeNDAP (NASA Earthdata), SQLite; React + Vite, three.js / React Three Fiber (3D farm), Leaflet with Esri World Imagery; Gemini API for the in-app assistant.

WHAT MAKES IT CREATIVE

It plans for one farmer's exact field rather than a whole region; it is honest about uncertainty (two NASA rain records disagree on monsoon onset, so it shows monthly risk instead of guessing a date); it stress-tests a plan before planting and learns from every real harvest; and every number is traced back to its NASA source.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

Water availability, soil health (bare days, nitrogen), pest-cycle breaks, market prices, farmer equipment and crop preferences, and data resolution (NASA POWER about 0.5°, IMERG 0.1°, GRACE-FO about 3°). FieldShift supports, not replaces, the farmer's judgment: every plan should be checked with the local Sub-Assistant Agriculture Officer (SAAO).

WHAT WE WOULD BUILD NEXT

Bangla voice and SMS advice for farmers without smartphones, field soil-test input, SMAP soil moisture and MODIS/Sentinel crop monitoring, and pilots with agriculture officers in Barind, haor and coastal districts.
